chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ziyad al-Nahdi, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr. He said:
Al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: It is sufficient as a victory from God for the believer that he sees his enemy acting in disobedience to God, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.حَسْبُ: Sufficient, enough — here meaning 'it is enough as a victory'
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — a formula of glorification for God
key_terms.مَعَاصِي: Acts of disobedience, sins — plural of ma'siya (transgression against God's commands)
key_terms.نُصْرَة: Victory, divine support, aid — God's help manifested through circumstances

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about seeing an enemy disobey God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that the true believer need not seek active revenge against his enemy, for it is sufficient that God's justice operates naturally — when the believer witnesses his enemy engaging in sin and disobedience, this itself represents divine support and a form of victory. This teaching reflects the Shia understanding of divine wisdom (hikma), where patience and trust in God's plan are the believer's weapons, and the enemy's spiritual degradation is a form of divine retribution.

en.bilal-muhammad: Al-Hasan b. Ibrahim b. Natana (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Abi Ziyad al-Nahdi from `Abdullah b. Bukayr. He said:
Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said: For a believer, it is enough of a victory from Allah to see his enemy disobeying Allah.
